posts.caption:
HAVE THE OILERS FOUND THEIR GOALIE? 🔥

Devon Levi was the first star last night, stopping 28 of 29 shots (.966) as Edmonton beat the Rangers 3-1 at Rogers Place. He was perfect at even strength (18 for 18) and on the penalty kill (10 for 10). The only goal against him came shorthanded.

Nine games into 2026-27, he’s 8-1-0 with a 2.75 GAA and a .898 save percentage.

It’s been a long road. He came up through the Carleton Place Canadians, then went to Northeastern, where he became the first goalie in NCAA history to win the Mike Richter Award twice. At the 2021 World Juniors he backstopped Canada to silver and was named the tournament’s best goaltender. Florida drafted him 212th overall in 2020, and his rights went to Buffalo in the Sam Reinhart trade in July 2021. On July 1, 2026, the Oilers got him from the Sabres, along with a 2028 seventh-rounder, for a 2028 third.

That’s starting to look like a steal. The question isn’t going away. Have the Oilers FOUND THERE GOALIE?
